stream_discovery.id_source: The complete URL displayed after Settings > Advanced Settings > RTSP > Generate URL
stream_discovery.notes: This is user-mediated setup, not network discovery. Store the URL as one opaque credential; model/firmware selection happens before enabling it.

streams.auth: Per-camera username/password embedded in the app-generated full URL
streams.name: Legacy official RTSP (app-generated full URL)
streams.notes: stream_url is opaque and includes the generated scheme, credentials, camera host, port and path. No default_port is declared because Wyze's legacy article does not state one. Do not append /live, /stream0, 554, a nickname or any other guessed component.

discovery.none: No automatic discovery is documented for this legacy branch. Ask the user for the camera address and the complete RTSP URL generated by the Wyze app after the exact product/installed-version check. Do not scan for an assumed port 554 and do not build a path from the model or nickname.

identification.notes: Manually confirm product identity and exact app-reported installed version in the Wyze app. For standalone Cam v3 this is 4.61.0.3, not the 4.61.0.1 archive package version. No RTSP port is asserted here, so no port-based matcher exists. Model code alone is insufficient for WYZE_CAKP2JFUS: exclude Floodlight.

device.name: Wyze Cam (legacy official RTSP firmware)
device.notes:
SCOPE IS THREE PRODUCT/INSTALLED-FIRMWARE PAIRS ONLY: Cam v2 WYZEC1-JZ with installed version 4.28.4.49, standalone Cam v3 WYZE_CAKP2JFUS with installed version 4.61.0.3, and Cam Pan v1 WYZECP1_JEF with installed version 4.29.4.49. Product and app-reported installed version must both match. The standalone Cam v3 download/archive package is named 4.61.0.1, but Wyze's official beta thread says it installs and reports 4.61.0.3; archive_package_version is for download/hash selection only and is not an installed-version match. Cam v1, Pan v2/v3, Cam v4, Floodlight products (including products sharing WYZE_CAKP2JFUS), Doorbells, Outdoor cameras and every other model or firmware are excluded. In particular, the newer 2025 RTSP beta for Cam v3/Pan v3 is a different route and is not included.
Wyze provided RTSP as a separate firmware branch. Features added after the branch are absent; AI and other Cam Plus functions can be unstable. Wyze does not commit to ongoing branch maintenance and recommends this route only for full-time RTSP use. Flashing is an advanced alternative, not a normal troubleshooting or update step.
After the exact branch is installed, the Wyze app enables RTSP per camera, creates per-camera credentials and generates the complete URL. Consume that full URL as an opaque value. This spec deliberately invents no RTSP path, port, stream name or credential format beyond the vendor article. identify_only reflects this project's missing video player, not the documented feed's availability to an external RTSP client.

openness.notes: RTSP is a standard protocol, but only on the vendor's old separate branch for the exact variants above. Stock firmware coverage in wyze-bridge-camera.yaml is a different access path.

procedures.basis: Wyze's official Wyze Cam RTSP support article; not replayed here.
procedures.name: Enable RTSP and generate per-camera credentials in the Wyze app

steps.action: Open Settings > Advanced Settings > RTSP for an exact supported camera and turn RTSP on.
Create the per-camera username/password and select Generate URL.
steps.expect: The app displays the complete RTSP URL for that camera.

exclusivity.recovery: Serialize initial client setup if the camera is unstable. Concurrent player limits are not established. If credentials are lost, use the app's RTSP settings to reset/recreate them and generate a fresh URL.

pairing.notes: App-layer RTSP credentials are independent of the camera's Wyze account binding. Nothing in this spec authorizes flashing or playback for any other model/firmware pair.

pin.notes: The owner chooses a separate RTSP username/password for each camera in the Wyze app. The app then generates the full URL carrying those credentials. No camera-wide default credential or URL path is claimed.

unpair.clears: RTSP access when disabled or when replacement credentials are generated; immediate revocation of every copied old URL is unverified.
unpair.notes: Turn RTSP off in the app to stop the service. To revoke a leaked URL, recreate the per-camera credentials and generate a new URL, then verify the old one fails; the precise revocation timing is not established.

issued_to_client: Per-camera RTSP username/password embedded in the app-generated full URL
Complete opaque stream_url, which is itself a secret
credentials.notes: The legacy article does not use the docker bridge's WB_API or the Wyze developer API key for playback. Treat the generated URL as a secret; do not log its embedded credentials or commit a real URL.
stored_on_device: Per-camera RTSP username/password created in the Wyze app

factory_reset.effect: Deletes the camera settings file and returns the matching camera to setup. Remove the microSD card first. This does not document a reset for Cam v1, Floodlight, Pan v2/v3 or any other excluded product.

procedures.basis: Wyze factory-reset article for Cam v1/v2/v3/Pan v1, restricted here to the two RTSP variants.
procedures.indicator: Solid yellow changes to blinking yellow.
procedures.name: Cam v2 or Pan v1 Setup button held for 10 seconds

steps.action: Remove any microSD card. With the Cam v2 or Pan v1 powered, hold its bottom Setup button for 10 seconds.
Release and wait at least 30 seconds, allowing up to five minutes, until the light changes from solid yellow to blinking yellow.

procedures.basis: Wyze factory-reset article for Cam v1/v2/v3/Pan v1, restricted to the standalone v3 RTSP variant.
procedures.name: Standalone Cam v3 Setup button held for 10 seconds

steps.action: Confirm this is a standalone Cam v3, not Floodlight. Remove any microSD card and hold the powered camera's bottom Setup button for 10 seconds.
Release and wait at least 30 seconds, allowing up to five minutes, until the status light turns red and the camera is ready to set up again.

cloud.local_alternative: After the app generates the URL, an RTSP player uses the camera on the local network. There is no documented app-free way to enable RTSP or mint the per-camera credentials on this branch.

methods.description: For a camera already reporting one of the three exact installed versions in device.variants. Confirm the variant, enable RTSP in the vendor app, choose per-camera credentials, and save the generated complete URL. Standalone Cam v3 must report installed version 4.61.0.3; its 4.61.0.1 archive package version is not a selection match.
methods.name: Already on the exact RTSP branch: enable in Wyze app

steps.action: Match both product_name/model and firmware.installed_version to one device.variants entry; reject every other model or installed version, including standalone Cam v3 reporting only archive version 4.61.0.1.
In the Wyze app, open the camera's live view, then Settings > Advanced Settings > RTSP, and let the app confirm firmware compatibility.
Turn on RTSP and create a username and password unique to this camera. The vendor article specifies 4-10 characters using lowercase letters and digits without special characters.
Select Generate URL and copy the complete URL shown by the app into the RTSP client as opaque stream_url, including its credentials, host, port and path.
steps.expect: The exact app-generated full URL is stored without constructing or normalizing any component.

steps.action: Open that URL with an RTSP-capable player on the same local network.
steps.expect: A live feed, if the camera/network supports it; no feed or resulting state has been replayed by this project.

methods.advanced_reason: Replaces camera firmware with an old separate branch. Later features are lost, AI/Cam Plus functions may be unstable, ongoing maintenance is not committed, and interrupted-flash recovery is unknown. Use only the exact product archive and hashes; this is not routine troubleshooting.
methods.description: Warning: this historical official installation route replaces camera firmware with an old separate branch. Later features are lost, AI/Cam Plus functions may be unstable, ongoing branch maintenance is not committed, and interrupted-flash recovery is unknown. Use only the exact product archive and hashes; this is not routine troubleshooting. It remains an alternative rather than role=historical because the official downloads still resolved during review. The second stage is the same app-enable route as primary.
methods.name: Advanced legacy microSD flash, then app enable

stages.description: Warning: later features are lost, AI/Cam Plus functions may be unstable, ongoing branch maintenance is not committed, and interrupted-flash recovery is unknown. Wyze recommends a 32 GB FAT32 microSD card. Select only the variant's archive, verify both published SHA-256 values, and use its exact microSD filename.
stages.name: Flash the exact official package from microSD

steps.action: Confirm the exact product and use its firmware.archive_package_version only to select firmware.archive_url for download and hash verification. Do not compare that archive version with the app-reported installed version or use another model's archive.
Verify the downloaded ZIP's archive_sha256, extract only its named inner binary, and verify inner_sha256 before putting it on the card.
steps.expect: Both hashes match the values independently recorded from Wyze's official host.

steps.action: Put the inner binary at the microSD root using the variant's microsd_filename: demo.bin for Cam v2/Pan v1, demo_wcv3.bin for standalone Cam v3.
Unplug the camera and insert the card. Hold Setup while reconnecting power; release at the variant's flash_indicator (lighter/yellowish blue for v2/Pan v1, purple for v3).
Wait three to four minutes for the flash/reboot and status-light changes, then remove the microSD card before ordinary use.
steps.expect: The camera returns in the Wyze app, normally retaining its prior account binding; an unpaired camera must be set up again.

cloud.local_alternative: After the app generates the URL, playback is local to the camera. There is no documented app-free way to enable RTSP or create the per-camera credentials on this legacy branch.

stages.description: Repeat the primary method's app steps; flashing alone does not enable a stream or create credentials.
stages.name: Enable RTSP and generate the full URL

steps.action: Confirm the app-reported installed firmware exactly matches the variant's firmware.installed_version: 4.61.0.3 for standalone Cam v3, not its 4.61.0.1 archive_package_version. Then open Settings > Advanced Settings > RTSP in the Wyze app.
Enable RTSP, choose the per-camera username/password, and select Generate URL.
Store and use the complete generated URL verbatim as stream_url; do not infer a default port or path.

setup.notes: Enabling RTSP and generating credentials requires the Wyze app/account. If the exact branch is not already installed, the alternative microSD route replaces firmware and carries feature-loss and maintenance risks.

rejoin.notes: Use the matching model's Wyze app setup/reconnect flow first. If a reset is necessary, use only its procedure above. Afterward confirm the exact firmware.installed_version remains app-reported, re-enable RTSP if needed, and replace stream_url only with the URL the app generates.

evidence.documentation_review: Wyze's official RTSP article supplies the branch limitation, feature-loss and maintenance warning, app enable flow, per-camera credential constraints and Generate URL behavior. The official flash article supplies microSD filenames, button/LED behavior and card removal. Official release posts identify the v2/Pan package versions. The official standalone v3 beta thread identifies archive package 4.61.0.1 and its app-reported installed version 4.61.0.3 as distinct values. No stream path or port is published in those legacy instructions.
evidence.open_questions: Actual stream reliability, concurrent-player limits, credential revocation timing, interrupted-flash recovery and current app behavior remain unverified.

dfu_mode.notes: Cam v2/Pan v1 show the documented lighter/yellowish solid blue; standalone Cam v3 shows solid purple. No network control surface is claimed during flashing.
